objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how old are you, and when did the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions start? Doctor: Where exactly are the lesions (face/torso/limbs/genitals), and do they look like blisters/ulcers with any crusting or are they just red bumps? Doctor: Have you had any recent injury, insect/tick bite, new meds, or contact with someone with a similar rash?

Patient: I’m 17, and the left wrist pain started about 3 days ago and got much worse this morning; I’ve had chills and feeling unwell since then. The lesions are on both wrists and hands—painless, purplish bumps that look like vesicles/pustules, without any crusting or sores elsewhere. I didn’t have any injury or new medications, and I can’t say I had a tick bite, but I did just come back from camping in Minnesota.

Doctor: On a scale of 0–10, how bad is the wrist pain, and can you move your wrist/fingers normally or is it swollen/hot? Any numbness, redness tracking up the arm, or swollen lymph nodes/armpits? Also, have you had sore throat, cough, or mouth/eye symptoms, and are you taking anything for the fever?

“It’s about a 9 out of 10, and the wrist is swollen and very tender—moving it hurts a lot, but I can still wiggle my fingers; there’s no numbness. I haven’t noticed redness streaking up my arm or swollen lymph nodes in my armpits, and I haven’t had sore throat, cough, or any mouth or eye symptoms. I’ve only been resting and haven’t taken any fever medicine yet.”

Doctor: I’m concerned about a severe infectious process on the wrists—could you tell me if the skin over the swollen area is warm, and whether you have any darkening/necrotic-looking centers in the purplish vesicles? Also, have you had a headache or stiff neck, and do you feel any joint pain beyond the left wrist?

It feels warm over the swollen left wrist, and the purplish bumps don’t have any dark or necrotic centers that I can see. I haven’t had a headache or stiff neck, and the only major joint pain is the left wrist—other than the knee pain from last week that went away.

Doctor: I’m going to request a few urgent tests—REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff, CRP_ESR, blood_cultures_before_antibiotics, and REQUEST TEST: Left_wrist_ultrasound_or_MRI_for_abscess_and_cellulitis (plus consider a skin swab/PCR for HSV/VZV and monkeypox if available). Doctor: While we wait, did you have any similar rash lesions elsewhere besides both wrists/hands (especially on face/genitals), and is there any tingling/burning pain in the area or only tenderness?

RESULTS: - Vital Signs: Temp 37.7°C (99.9°F); BP 120/80 mmHg; HR 80 bpm; RR 14/min - Skin Exam: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on dorsum of both wrists/hands; 2 lesions on left palm - Musculoskeletal Exam: Left wrist swelling, erythema, severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement - CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated); Hemoglobin 14 g/dL; Platelets 300,000 /μL - Left Wrist Joint Aspiration: Synovial WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated); Gram stain: gram-negative diplococci seen - Blood Cultures: Pending - STI Screen: Gonorrhea positive; Chlamydia negative; HIV negative

Doctor: With the Gram stain showing gram-negative diplococci in the wrist joint fluid plus synovial WBC >50,000 and high peripheral WBC, I’m most concerned about **gonococcal septic arthritis** (disseminated gonococcal infection) causing the violaceous vesiculopustular hand/wrist lesions. Do you have any urethral discharge, pelvic/testicular pain, abnormal vaginal bleeding/discharge, or recent new sexual partners (and have your lesions ever been biopsied or tested by PCR)? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: GC/CT NAAT from any genital/cervical samples available (if not already), and REQUEST TEST: HIV already done—now also REQUEST TEST: repeat/confirm NAAT from lesion swab for Neisseria gonorrhoeae (if available) and do a full joint exam to check for other joints. Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: **Disseminated gonococcal infection causing gonococcal septic arthritis of the left wrist with vesiculopustular/violaceous lesions**
